requirement:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Given the following project structure:

 - Project A
    - `ProjectA.MyType`

 - Project B
    - References
        - Project A
    - Package References
        - MessagePack
    
I need to have a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for type `ProjectA.MyType` generated **inside Project B** instead of Project A, because the latter has no (and cannot have) reference to MessagePack nuget package.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that will work for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.

For example:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

That's it. The class does not even need to declare a body (no `{` and `}`), because the actual implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:

1 - Use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes. This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

2 - Allow the generator and analyzers to work with user-defined versions of the MessagePack attributes. This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`. With this, I could simply copy and paste the attribute definitions for MessagePack attributes such as `[Key]` into my Project A, and have the source-generated formatter (as described above) pick them.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly. This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency. Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.

## Motivation

Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal. It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

story.summary: Adds a public `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute to MessagePack.Annotations. A user marks a `partial` class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>` with it, and the source generator writes that class's body and registers it in `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. `T` can live in an assembly that does not reference MessagePack. By default the formatter is contractless: public read-write instance members go in a string-keyed map, ordered by name. An optional `SurrogateType` names a type whose `[Key]`/`[IgnoreMember]` attributes set the keys; its members must match `T`'s members by name and type. Four new error diagnostics (MsgPack019–022) cover misuse. Both formatter templates now emit `partial class` for these user-declared formatters. A new test library without a MessagePack reference, execution tests and generator diagnostic tests come with it.

findings.description: Claim C4 disputed: Over-citation and requirement only partly met: (1) Cited GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L116-119 includes L117 (Formatter = new QualifiedNamedTypeName(formatter)), which overrides the default resolver-nested formatter name so the generated partial class targets the user's type and namespace, and no claim describes L117. (2) The quoted requirement asks for bodyless semicolon syntax ('partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;' with no '{' and '}'), which is invalid C# for a class without a primary constructor parameter list '()' unless declared as a record class—and record declarations are ignored by ClassDeclarationSyntax filters on MessagePackGenerator.cs L31 and GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L297, with no test covering bodyless declarations.

Claim C7 disputed: The named test ContractlessStructRoundTrips only exercises a struct (ExternalPoint) and does not test the second half of the claim—that classes require an accessible parameterless constructor or else raise NoDeserializingConstructor on GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L77-81. No test in the diff triggers L79, and Diagnostic.Create(MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.NoDeserializingConstructor, location) passes zero message arguments without verifying NoDeserializingConstructor.MessageFormat (not shown in diff).

Claim C8 disputed: Over-citation: C8 cites GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L104-115 (the entire ObjectSerializationInfo.Create call setting nestedFormatterRequired, genericTypeParameters, constructorParameters, isIntKey, members, hasIMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver, needsCastOnAfter, needsCastOnBefore, and resolverOptions), whereas the claim only explains passing isClass on L106.

Claim C9 disputed: Over-citation: C9 cites GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L143-179, which includes L171-179 reporting MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.MemberNeedsKey and returning null when a non-ignored surrogate member lacks a [Key(int)] or [Key(string)] attribute. Neither C9 nor any other claim describes L171-179, and no test covers it.

Claim C19 disputed: Wrong citation for half the claim and understated bug: setting nestedFormatterRequired: false and constructorParameters: Array.Empty<MemberSerializationInfo>() occurs on GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs L104-115, not in the cited L83-86 or L121-126. Furthermore, on L84-85, m.ExplicitInterfaceImplementations.Length > 0 && (m.Name == "OnBeforeSerialize" || m.Name == "OnAfterDeserialize") is unconditionally false in Roslyn because explicit interface method symbols prefix m.Name with the interface name (e.g. "MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize"), and L84 also ignores base-type implementations and conflates needsCastOnBefore with needsCastOnAfter.

Claim C20 disputed: The test run failed to build ('TEST RUN: build-failed'), so the execution tests do not compile and run. Specifically, cited ExternalWidgetSurrogate (GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypes.cs L27-37) applies [Key] and [IgnoreMember] without [MessagePackObject] while MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer is not updated to exempt surrogates, and cited MessagePack.SourceGenerator.ExternalTypes.csproj L9 hardcodes TargetFramework net8.0. In addition, REQ-2129's Union/attribute support for external types is only partly met because surrogates do not support Union.

Claim C26 disputed: Cited documentation contradicts the implementation in three places: (1) doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md L26 states that nesting types containing the formatter must also be declared partial, but GeneratedFormatterCollector.IsPartial (L293-299) never checks ContainingType, so MsgPack019 is not reported and the generator emits uncompilable C# (CS0260); (2) README.md L1656 says read-only members are skipped because they cannot be deserialized, whereas init-only properties pass IsPublicReadWrite (L279-281) and are serialized/deserialized; (3) README.md L1663-1673 and MsgPack022.md L9-13 show surrogate classes with [Key]/[IgnoreMember] and no [MessagePackObject], which MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer does not exempt.

needsCast compares `m.Name` with "OnBeforeSerialize"/"OnAfterDeserialize" on explicit interface implementations. Roslyn names explicit implementations with the interface prefix (e.g. "MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize"), so this never matches. A type that implements the callbacks explicitly would get generated code calling `value.OnBeforeSerialize()` without a cast, which fails to compile.

IsPartial checks only the formatter's own declaration. If the formatter is nested in a non-partial type, the generator still emits nesting types, and the user gets raw compiler errors instead of MsgPack019, although the docs (MsgPack019.md line 26) say containing types must be partial. Formatter accessibility (e.g. a private nested formatter the resolver cannot reach) is not checked either.

Raising the analyzer Roslyn dependency to 4.14.0 raises the minimum Visual Studio/SDK version needed to load the MessagePack analyzer/generator for all users. The requirement does not call for it and the diff gives no reason.

GetInstanceMembers(surrogate) includes private fields and properties. Any surrogate member, including private helpers, without [Key] or [IgnoreMember] stops generation with MemberNeedsKey. This is stricter than the docs suggest.

Nothing stops two [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes for the same T, or one targeting a type that already has [MessagePackObject]. Both would be added to the resolver, and the outcome (duplicate registration or compile error) is untested.

The collector runs twice per formatter, once for the model and once for diagnostics. The incremental pipeline also carries INamedTypeSymbol values, which defeats caching across compilations. This is a performance cost, not a correctness issue.

Raising MicrosoftCodeAnalysisVersion to 4.14.0 only when '$(IsAnalyzerProject)'=='true' while leaving line 9 at 4.12.0 (with CentralPackageTransitivePinningEnabled=true on line 6) causes NuGet package downgrade NU1605 / assembly version conflict CS1705 in non-analyzer projects such as MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests that reference MessagePack.SourceGenerator, breaking the build. Shipping an analyzer referencing Roslyn 4.14.0 also breaks consumers on SDKs/Visual Studio older than VS 17.14 / .NET 9.0.300.

MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer is not updated to exempt surrogate types referenced via [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(...))] from TypeMustBeMessagePackObject, so surrogate classes carrying [Key] and [IgnoreMember] without [MessagePackObject] (such as ExternalWidgetSurrogate in GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypes.cs L27) trigger analyzer errors whenever MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer runs. In addition, MsgPack019-MsgPack022 are advertised in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.SupportedDiagnostics (L382-385) without being analyzed in Initialize.

MessagePack.SourceGenerator.ExternalTypes.csproj hardcodes <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework> instead of netstandard2.0, which breaks restore/build with NU1201 for any non-net8.0 target framework (such as net472) in the referencing MessagePack.SourceGenerator.ExecutionTests project.

Collect validates the formatted data type T, but never checks whether the user-declared formatter class itself is generic (formatter.IsGenericType), abstract (formatter.IsAbstract), or missing an accessible parameterless constructor, nor does IsPartial (L293) verify that enclosing types of a nested formatter are partial. Any of these cases bypasses diagnostics and emits uncompilable C# in the formatter or GeneratedMessagePackResolver.

CreateSurrogateMembers accepts any int [Key] value via 'key is not (int or string)', including negative integers such as [Key(-1)]. Negative int keys are passed directly into CreateMember (L207) without a >= 0 check, causing FormatterTemplate to emit broken array header lengths and unreachable negative switch cases.

When T declares C# 11 'required' members that are omitted or marked [IgnoreMember] on a surrogate (or skipped by IsPublicReadWrite due to non-public init/set accessors), no diagnostic is reported and the generated formatter's 'new T { ... }' initializer fails C# compilation with CS9035.

Multiple [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes targeting the same type T (or a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] targeting a type that also carries [MessagePackObject]) are not diagnosed; either one formatter is silently dropped by ImmutableSortedSet (leaving a partial class with unimplemented IMessagePackFormatter<T> methods, CS0535) or duplicate entries are emitted into GeneratedMessagePackResolver.

The accessible parameterless constructor check is gated on 'isClass', so a C# 10+ struct in another assembly declaring a private or internal parameterless constructor is accepted without a diagnostic and fails to compile with CS0122 when the generated formatter invokes 'new T()'.

Casting the SurrogateType named argument via 'as INamedTypeSymbol' turns non-named type arguments (such as typeof(MyType[]), an IArrayTypeSymbol) into null, causing the generator to silently fall back to contractless mode instead of reporting an invalid surrogate diagnostic.

Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.
Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal.
It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.
